reply.text:
This error means Git found two sets of commits that share no common ancestor, so it can't work out how to combine them. Git refuses by default because this usually means you're joining two unrelated projects, which would be a mistake.

It often happens when:

- You ran `git init`, made commits locally, then added a remote that already has its own history and tried to pull or merge.
- You're combining two separately created repositories.
- A remote was recreated or replaced, so its history no longer connects to your clone.

To see what you have, run:

```
git log --oneline --all --graph
git remote -v
```

Then choose a fix based on which history you want to keep:

- **If the two histories really belong together** (for example, you started a local copy and the remote is the same project), you can force the merge:
  ```
  git pull --allow-unrelated-histories
  ```
  Resolve any conflicts it reports, since the two sides were never merged before.

- **If your local repo has nothing you need**, it's usually cleaner to discard it and clone or reset to the remote:
  ```
  git fetch origin
  git reset --hard origin/main
  ```
  This deletes local commits that aren't on the remote, so check first that you don't need them. Replace `main` with your branch name if it differs.

- **If you're not sure**, back up the local work first, for example with `git branch backup-local`, before choosing either option.

If you paste the output of the two commands above, I can tell you which case you're in.
